rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening means that many generations were destroyed after Noah, including ʿĀd and Thamūd.
rows.anchor: من بعد نوح } كعاد وثمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about generations explains and specifies the preceding word meaning “how many.”
rows.anchor: القرون } بيان لكم وتمييز له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God fully apprehends servants’ hidden and outward sins and punishes them; “all-aware” precedes “all-seeing” because its object comes first.
rows.anchor: يدرك بواطنها وظواهرها فيعاقب عليها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person seeking the immediate life has made it his sole concern.
rows.anchor: مقصورا عليها همه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly grant is restricted by God’s will and choice, since no one receives every wish or all that they desire; this teaches that achievement and concern are gifts.
rows.anchor: لا يجد كل متمن ما يتمناه، ولا كل واجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the phrase “and for whom We will,” the prepositional phrase substitutes for “to him” as a partitive apposition.
rows.anchor: بدل من له بدل البعض.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has “what He wills,” with the pronoun referring to God so it agrees with the common reading.
rows.anchor: يشاء» والضمير فيه لله تعالى حتى يطابق المشهورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes “for whom” as a restriction to the person God specifically wills to grant.
rows.anchor: فيكون مخصوصا بمن أراد الله تعالى به ذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported interpretation applies the verse to hypocrites who joined Muslims in raids for a share of the spoils, not religious purpose.
rows.anchor: وقيل الآية في المنافقين كانوا يراءون المسلمين ويغزون معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly seeker is cast into Hell, disgraced and driven away from God’s mercy.
rows.anchor: مطرودا من رحمة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proper effort for the afterlife means doing what is commanded and avoiding what is forbidden, rather than inventing acts of devotion.
rows.anchor: وهو الإتيان بما أمر به، والانتهاء عما نهى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition in “strives for it” signals intention and sincerity.
rows.anchor: وفائدة اللام اعتبار النية والإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith must be sound, without either associating partners with God or denial; it is the essential condition.
rows.anchor: إيمانا صحيحا لا شرك معه ولا تكذيب فإنه العمدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who meet the three conditions have effort accepted by God and recompensed; God’s thanking obedience means rewarding it.
rows.anchor: من الله تعالى أي مقبولا عنده مثابا عليه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Both” means each of the two groups, and its nunation stands in place of a genitive complement.
rows.anchor: كل واحد من الفريقين، والتنوين بدل من المضاف إليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God repeatedly extends gifts, making each new grant support what came before.
rows.anchor: بالعطاء مرة بعد أخرى ونجعل آنفه مددا لسالفه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “These and those” is an appositive to “both”; “from your Lord’s gift” attaches to “We extend.”
rows.anchor: من معطاه متعلق ب { نمد }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s worldly gift is not withheld from either believer or unbeliever, as an act of grace.
rows.anchor: ممنوعا لا يمنعه في الدنيا من مؤمن ولا كافر تفضلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly differences being compared are differences in provision; “how” is accusative as a circumstantial expression with “We favored.”
rows.anchor: في الرزق، وانتصاب { كيف } ب { فضلنا } على الحال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife has greater disparities, through the levels of Paradise and the depths of Hell.
rows.anchor: أي التفاوت في الآخرة أكبر، لأن التفاوت فيها بالجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address against associating another god is directed to the Prophet with his community intended, or to everyone.
rows.anchor: الخطاب للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم والمراد به أمته أو لكل أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You would sit” may mean becoming something, as a sharpened blade becomes spear-like, or becoming unable, as in the idiom “he sat back from it.”
rows.anchor: فتصير من قولهم شحذ الشفرة حتى قعدت كأنها حربة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolater gathers blame from angels and believers and abandonment from God; by implication, the monotheist is praised and supported.
rows.anchor: جامعا على نفسك الذم من الملائكة والمؤمنين والخذلان من الله تعالى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your Lord decreed” means He issued a command that is definitive.
rows.anchor: وأمر أمرا مقطوعا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction can be read as “that you worship none but Him,” with an elided preposition, or with “that” explanatory and “do not” prohibitive.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون { ءان } مفسرة و { لا } ناهية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exclusive worship belongs only to the one of ultimate greatness and beneficence; this elaborates the effort for the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وهو كالتفصيل لسعي الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parental-duty phrase can mean “that you do good to parents,” or an imperative to treat them well; parents are the apparent cause of existence and sustenance.
rows.anchor: وبأن تحسنوا، أو وأحسنوا بالوالدين إحسانا لأنهما السبب الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition cannot attach to “goodness,” because that word’s complement cannot precede it.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن تتعلق الباء بالإحسان لأن صلته لا تتقدم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “If either or both reach old age with you” uses a conditional particle reinforced by “ma,” permitting the emphatic nun; “either” is the subject of “reach.”
rows.anchor: أما } هي إن الشرطية زيدت عليها ما تأكيدا ولذلك صح لحوق النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading of Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī, “they both reach,” refers the verb to the parents; “both” is coordinated with or substitutes for “either,” not an emphatic of the dual alif.
rows.anchor: على قراءة حمزة والكسائي من ألف «يبلغان» الراجع إلى «الوالدين»،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “With you” means that the parents are in the child’s care and keeping.
rows.anchor: أن يكونا في كنفك وكفالتك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Uff” forbids expressing annoyance at what is unpleasant in parents or resenting their care; it is a sound of irritation, or a word meaning “I am annoyed.”
rows.anchor: فلا تتضجر مما يستقذر منهما وتستثقل من مؤنتهما، وهو صوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word “uff” is built on kasra at the meeting of two vowelless letters; Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ nunate it as indefinite, while Ibn Kathīr, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Yaʿqūb read it with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وهو مبني على الكسر لالتقاء الساكنين وتنوينه في قراءة نافع وحفص للتنكير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further readings have it with fatḥa and nunation or with ḍamma by assimilation, either nunated or unnunated.
rows.anchor: وقرىء به منونا وبالضم للاتباع كمنذ منونا وغير منون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If even this minor expression is forbidden, all other forms of harm are forbidden by a fortiori reasoning.
rows.anchor: والنهي عن ذلك يدل على المنع من سائر أنواع الايذاء قياسا بطريق الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An idiom likens a person lacking even the smallest thing to one who lacks the tiny naqīr and qiṭmīr; the Prophet prevented Ḥudhayfa from killing his father among the polytheists.
rows.anchor: منع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حذيفة من قتل أبيه وهو في صف المشركين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After commanding kindness, the passage forbids whatever would hurt parents.
rows.anchor: نهى عما يؤذيهما بعد الأمر بالإحسان بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do not rebuke them” means do not harshly scold them for what displeases you; nahy, nahr, and nahm are related words.
rows.anchor: ولا تزجرهما عما لا يعجبك بإغلاظ. وقيل النهي والنهر والنهم أخوات.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Speak to them graciously” replaces sighing and rebuke, requiring kind words without harshness.
rows.anchor: بدل التأفيف والنهر. { قولا كريما } جميلا لا شراسة فيه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lowering the wing of humility means being submissive and humble toward parents.
rows.anchor: تذلل لهما وتواضع فيهما

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: The cited verse uses a hand for the north wind and a bridle for the cold, supporting the metaphorical assignment of a wing.
rows.anchor: وجعل للذل جناحا كما جعل لبيد في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wing may be lowered as emphatic imagery, or “your wing” is intended as in the command to lower one’s wing to believers.
rows.anchor: وأمره بخفضه مبالغة أو أراد جناحه كقوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive “wing of humility” explains and intensifies the image; it means your own humbled wing.
rows.anchor: وإضافته إلى الذل للبيان والمبالغة كما أضيف حاتم إلى الجود،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with kasra in “humility” means obedience; its adjective is “submissive.”
rows.anchor: وقرىء «الذل» بالكسر وهو الانقياد والنعت منه ذلول.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Out of mercy” is intense compassion for parents who now need the child, after once being utterly dependent on them.
rows.anchor: من فرط رحمتك عليهما لافتقارهما إلى من كان أفقر خلق الله تعالى إليهما بالأمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ask God to grant lasting mercy rather than relying on one’s temporary compassion; even unbelieving parents may be shown mercy through guidance.
rows.anchor: وادع الله تعالى أن يرحمهما برحمته الباقية، ولا تكتف برحمتك الفانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks for mercy like the parents’ care, upbringing, and guidance in childhood, fulfilling God’s promise to the merciful.
rows.anchor: رحمة مثل رحمتهما علي وتربيتهما وإرشادهما لي في صغري وفاء بوعدك للراحمين

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A man asked whether serving his aged parents as they had served him in childhood repaid them; the Prophet said no, because they had wanted him to live while he wants them to die.
rows.anchor: روي: أن رجلا قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن أبوي بلغا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows whether one intends kindness and honors parents, warning against inward resentment and burdening oneself with their care.
rows.anchor: من قصد البر إليهما واعتقاد ما يجب لهما من التوقير،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being righteous means intending righteousness.
rows.anchor: قاصدين للصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The penitent” are those who turn repeatedly in repentance; God forgives failures arising from distress or lapses that hurt parents, a severe warning.
rows.anchor: ما فرط منهم عند حرج الصدر من أذية أو تقصير، وفيه تشديد عظيم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may generally concern every repentant person, including one who repents after wronging parents because it follows that discussion.
rows.anchor: يندرج فيه الجاني على أبويه التائب من جنايته لوروده على أثره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A relative’s due includes maintaining kinship, good companionship, and kindness.
rows.anchor: من صلة الرحم وحسن المعاشرة والبر عليهم

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa says poor relatives who are unmarriageable kin have a right to financial support.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: حقهم إذا كانوا محارم فقراء أن ينفق عليهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the relatives as the Prophet’s own kin.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بذي القربى أقارب الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waste is spending money on improper things and extravagant outlay; the root sense of tabdhīr is scattering.
rows.anchor: بصرف المال فيما لا ينبغي وإنفاقه على وجه الإسراف، وأصل التبذير التفريق.

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told Saʿd that using even a flowing river does not make extravagance in ablution acceptable.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال لسعد وهو يتوضأ:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Brothers of Satan” may mean those resembling him in evil, since waste and destruction are evil.
rows.anchor: أمثالهم في الشرارة فإن التضييع والاتلاف شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they are Satan’s companions and followers, obeying him in extravagance and spending on sins.
rows.anchor: أصدقاءهم وأتباعهم لأنهم يطيعونهم في الإسراف والصرف في المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says they slaughtered camels, gambled shares in them, and squandered wealth for reputation; God forbade this and commanded charitable spending.
rows.anchor: روي: أنهم كانوا ينحرون الإبل ويتياسرون عليها ويبذرون أموالهم في السمعة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan is intensely ungrateful to his Lord, so should not be obeyed.
rows.anchor: مبالغا في الكفر به فينبغي أن لا يطاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition addresses killing children from fear of poverty, especially burying daughters; God promises provision for parents and children, since killing them gravely interrupts procreation and the human species.
rows.anchor: مخافة الفاقة، وقتلهم أولادهم هو وأدهم بناتهم مخافة الفقر فنهاهم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase calls the act a grave sin; the word khāṭiʾ means sin, while Ibn ʿĀmir reads khaṭʾ, a noun from akhṭaʾ opposite to correctness or a dialect form.
rows.anchor: الاثم يقال خطىء خطأ كأثم إثما، وقرأ ابن عامر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads khaṭāʾ with long alif and kasra, either as a dialect form or a verbal noun from khāṭaʾ, attested by a cited line; other variants include long fatḥa and forms without hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير «خطاء» بالمد والكسر وهو إما لغة فيه أو مصدر خاطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Avoiding adultery includes avoiding intent and its preliminaries, let alone the act itself.
rows.anchor: بالعزم والإتيان بالمقدمات فضلا عن أن تباشروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adultery is an exceptionally ugly deed and a vile path: sexual usurpation that disrupts lineage and stirs conflict.
rows.anchor: وبئس طريقا طريقه، وهو الغصب على الابضاع المؤدي إلى قطع الأنساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lawful grounds for killing are apostasy after faith, adultery after chastity, and intentional killing of an inviolable believer.
rows.anchor: إلا بإحدى ثلاث: كفر بعد إيمان: وزنا بعد إحصان، وقتل مؤمن معصوم عمدا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person killed wrongfully did not deserve death; the victim’s guardian is the heir who assumes his affairs after death.
rows.anchor: غير مستوجب للقتل. { فقد جعلنا لوليه } للذي يلي أمره بعد وفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardian’s authority may mean power to hold the killer accountable or to exact retaliation; “wronged” proves intentional aggression because accidental killing is not called injustice.
rows.anchor: تسلطا بالمؤاخذة بمقتضى القتل على من عليه، أو بالقصاص على القاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do not exceed bounds in killing” may address the killer, forbidding killing anyone without entitlement, or the guardian, forbidding mutilation or killing someone other than the killer.
rows.anchor: بأن يقتل من لا يستحق قتله، فإن العاقل لا يفعل ما يعود عليه بالهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ubayy’s plural reading supports addressing the killer; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read a singular form addressed to one of the two parties.
rows.anchor: ويؤيد الأول قراءة أبي «فلا تسرفوا». وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «فلا تسرف»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He is supported” may refer to the victim, supported by retaliation in this world and reward in the next; the guardian, whose retaliation right God established and authorities must aid; or an overreaching killer’s victim, since the killer faces retaliation, discipline, and sin.
rows.anchor: والضمير إما للمقتول فإنه منصور في الدنيا بثبوت القصاص بقتله وفي الآخرة بالثواب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not even approach an orphan’s property, much less transact with it, except by the best method; reaching maturity ends the permission to manage it.
rows.anchor: فضلا أن تتصرفوا فيه. { إلا بالتى هى أحسن } إلا بالطريقة التي هي أحسن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant may be duties God imposed or any other covenant; it is demanded of the party to fulfill it, or the breaker is questioned and rebuked, or the covenant itself is personified as questioned, like the buried girl.
rows.anchor: بما عاهدكم الله من تكاليفه، أو ما عاهدتموه وغيره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may instead mean that the person who made the covenant will be questioned.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد أن صاحب العهد كان مسؤولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Give full measure without shortchanging.
rows.anchor: ولا تبخسوا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qisṭās is a balanced scale; although Greek in origin, a foreign word becomes Arabic when Arabs inflect and use it as their own, so its presence does not impugn the Qur’an’s Arabic.
rows.anchor: بالميزان السوي، وهو رومي عرب ولا يقدح ذلك في عربية القرآن،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ read the qāf with kasra here and in al-Shuʿarāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص بكسر القاف هنا وفي «الشعراء».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Better in outcome” uses taʾwīl from āla, “to return,” and means a better consequence.
rows.anchor: وأحسن عاقبة تفعيل من آل إذا رجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb means do not follow; an alternate form derives from following someone’s tracks, the root of qāfa, the tracker of lineages.
rows.anchor: ولا تتبع وقرىء { ولا تقف } من قاف أثره إذا قفاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not follow what is unsupported by knowledge, whether through blind imitation or guessing.
rows.anchor: ما لم يتعلق به علمك تقليدا أو رجما بالغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who prohibit following conjecture cite this verse; the answer is that knowledge can mean a well-supported, predominant belief, whether certain or probable, a common usage.
rows.anchor: واحتج به من منع اتباع الظن وجوابه أن المراد بالعلم هو الاعتقاد الراجح المستفاد من سند،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view restricts the prohibition to matters of creed.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه مخصوص بالعقائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation concerns shooting or false testimony, supported by a Prophetic warning that one who falsely accuses a believer is confined in the valley of corruption until cleared.
rows.anchor: وقيل بالرمي وشهادة الزور ويؤيده قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: الكميت
rows.claim: Al-Kumayt’s verse says he does not shoot the innocent without cause or accuse chaste women, illustrating the root’s use.
rows.anchor: وقول الكميت: ولا أرمي البريء بغير ذنب ولا أقفو الحواصن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hearing, sight, and heart are grouped with rational beings because they will be questioned about their states and testify against their owner; “those” can refer to non-rational things as a collective.
rows.anchor: أي كل هذه الأعضاء فأجراها مجرى العقلاء لما كانت مسؤولة عن أحوالها شاهدة على صاحبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “about it” may refer to each faculty, which is accountable for its owner’s use; alternatively it refers to the act of following or to the person whose senses are involved.
rows.anchor: ضمير كل أي كان كل واحد منها مسؤولا عن نفسه، يعني عما فعل به صاحبه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One grammatical view attaches “answerable” to “about it,” as in al-Fātiḥa 1:7, meaning the person will be asked about the faculties; al-Bayḍāwī rejects it because a verb and its substitute cannot precede their governing element.
rows.anchor: وقيل { مسؤولا } مسند إلى { عنه } كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that a person is accountable even for resolving to commit a sin.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن العبد مؤاخذ بعزمه على المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading of “the heart” changes hamza to wāw after ḍamma, then opens the resulting vowel.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { والفؤاد } بقلب الهمزة واوا بعد الضمة ثم إبدالها بالفتح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Walking arrogantly” means walking full of pride.
rows.anchor: أي ذا مرح وهو الاختيال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading marahan treats it as a verbal noun, more fitting to the ruling even though a verbal noun is more emphatic than a plain adjective.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { مرحا } وهو باعتبار الحكم أبلغ وإن كان المصدر آكد من صريح النعت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: You cannot tear a hole in the earth with the force of your tread or reach the mountains by strutting; this mocks the arrogant and explains that conceit is foolish and useless, unlike humility.
rows.anchor: لن تجعل فيها خرقا بشدة وطأتك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “All that” points to the twenty-five qualities listed beginning with the ban on associating another god.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى الخصال الخمس والعشرين المذكورة.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says these are the precepts written on Moses’ tablets.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما: أنها المكتوبة في ألواح موسى عليه السلام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Its evil” means the forbidden items, since the list contains both commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: يعني المنهي عنه فإن المذكورات مأمورات ومناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ḥijāzī and Baṣran readers read sayyiʾuhu as the predicate of “was,” taking “that” to refer specifically to what was prohibited; makrūhan may then be appositive, an adjective by meaning, or circumstantial.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحجازيان والبصريان { سيئه } على أنها خبر { كان } والاسم ضمير { كل }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Disliked by your Lord” means detested, the opposite of approved, not the opposite of willed, since all events occur by God’s will.
rows.anchor: والمراد به المبغوض المقابل للمرضى لا ما يقابل المراد لقيام القاطع على أن الحوادث كلها واقعة بإرادته تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior rulings are part of revealed wisdom: knowing truth for its own sake and goodness so that it may be practiced.
rows.anchor: معرفة الحق لذاته والخير للعمل به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated ban on associating another god marks monotheism as wisdom’s beginning and end: without it deeds are null, and effort aimed at or abandoned for another is lost; the first warning described worldly consequences and this one the hereafter.
rows.anchor: كرره للتنبيه على أن التوحيد مبدأ الأمر ومنتهاه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned person blames himself and is driven away from God’s mercy.
rows.anchor: تلوم نفسك. { مدحورا } مبعدا من رحمة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke addresses those who call angels God’s daughters: did God favor you with sons, the better children, while assigning daughters to Himself?
rows.anchor: خطاب لمن قالوا الملائكة بنات الله، والهمزة للإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim contradicts their own reason and custom.
rows.anchor: بنات لنفسه وهذا خلاف ما عليه عقولكم وعادتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is a grave claim to attribute children, characteristic of transient bodies, to God, to prefer oneself by assigning Him what one dislikes, and to abase the noble angels.
rows.anchor: بإضافة الأولاد إليه، وهي خاصة بعض الأجسام لسرعة زوالها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God repeats this meaning through different kinds of argument in passages of the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: كررنا هذا المعنى بوجوه من التقرير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “this Qur’an” means that the rejection of divine daughters has been elaborated throughout this subject.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بهذا القرآن إبطال إضافة البنات إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lightened reading omits the doubling in ṣarrafnā.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { صرفنا } بالتخفيف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose is that people take heed and remember; “what does it increase them except aversion” means withdrawal from truth and diminished reassurance.
rows.anchor: عن الحق وقلة طمأنينة إليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read the verb here and in al-Furqān with the form of dhikr, meaning recollection.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي هنا وفي الفرقان { ليذكروا } من الذكر الذي هو بمعنى التذكر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Ḥafṣ read the following verbs with yāʾ in this verse and the next; several other readers use that reading only in the second, distinguishing the address to polytheists from God’s own declaration of transcendence.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وحفص عن عاصم بالياء فيه وفيما بعده على أن الكلام مع الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If rival gods existed, they would seek a way to the Lord of the Throne either to contend for supremacy like kings or to draw near through obedience, recognizing His power and their own weakness.
rows.anchor: لطلبوا إلى من هو مالك الملك سبيلا بالمعازة كما يفعل الملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Glory to Him” declares God free of imperfection; “He is exalted” means far removed from their claims.
rows.anchor: ينزه تنزيها. { وتعالى عما يقولون علوا } تعاليا. { كبيرا } متباعدا غاية البعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God occupies the highest mode of existence, necessary and everlasting in Himself; begetting belongs to the lowest mode, beings whose survival is finite.
rows.anchor: فإنه في أعلى مراتب الوجود وهو كونه واجب الوجود والبقاء لذاته،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens, earth, and all things glorify God by their contingent, created state, which points to the eternal Creator.
rows.anchor: ينزهه عما هو من لوازم الإمكان وتوابع الحدوث بلسان الحال حيث تدل بإمكانها وحدوثها على الصانع القديم الواجب لذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists fail to understand this glorification because they neglect sound reflection.
rows.anchor: لإخلالكم بالنظر الصحيح الذي به يفهم تسبيحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, glorification can encompass both spoken praise and indication, attributed jointly to what can and cannot speak, if a word may carry both meanings.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يحمل التسبيح على المشترك بين اللفظ والدلالة لإسناده إلى ما يتصور منه اللفظ وإلى ما لا يتصور منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Ibn ʿĀmir, Nāfiʿ, and Abū Bakr read the verb with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر ونافع وأبو بكر «يسبح» بالياء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is forbearing by not hastening punishment for heedlessness and associating partners, and forgives those who repent.
rows.anchor: حيث لم يعاجلكم بالعقوبة على غفلتكم وشرككم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A barrier keeps those who disbelieve in the afterlife from understanding the Qur’an recited to them.
rows.anchor: يحجبهم عن فهم ما تقرؤه عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Veiled” may mean possessing a veil, by analogy with “His promise is fulfilled” and the expression “a rain-filled flood”; it may also mean hidden from the senses or concealed behind a second barrier.
rows.anchor: أو مستورا عن الحس، أو بحجاب آخر لا يفهمون ولا يفهمون أنهم لا يفهمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description also denies their awareness that they fail to understand, confirming their being stamped in misguidance, as the next verse makes explicit.
rows.anchor: نفى عنهم أن يفهموا ما أنزل عليهم من الآيات بعدما نفي عنهم التفقه للدلالات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coverings on their hearts hide them from perceiving and accepting truth.
rows.anchor: تكنها وتحول دونها عن إدراك الحق وقبوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “lest they understand” may express aversion to their understanding, or be the object of the implied action “We prevented them from understanding.”
rows.anchor: كراهة أن يفقهوه، ويجوز أن يكون مفعولا لما دل عليه قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deafness in their ears blocks listening; because the Qur’an is miraculous in both wording and meaning, deniers are described as obstructed from each.
rows.anchor: يمنعهم عن استماعه. ولما كان القرآن معجزا من حيث اللفظ والمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your Lord alone” means without their idols; waḥdahu is a circumstantial verbal noun meaning uniquely one.
rows.anchor: واحدا غير مشفوع به آلهتهم، مصدر وقع موقع الحال وأصله يحد وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They turn away from hearing the affirmation of oneness; “nufūran” may mean fleeing or be a plural of nāfir like qāʿid/qʿūd.
rows.anchor: هربا من استماع التوحيد ونفرة أو تولية، ويجوز أن يكون جمع نافر كقاعد وقعود.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows their motive for listening: mockery of the Prophet and the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: بسببه ولأجله من الهزء بك وبالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When they listen” and “when they confer privately” both depend on “We know”; they listen while concealing their aim and then whisper together.
rows.anchor: ظرف ل { أعلم } وكذا. { وإذ هم نجوى } أي نحن أعلم بغرضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najwā may be a verbal noun or a plural meaning whisperers.
rows.anchor: و { نجوى } مصدر ويحتمل أن يكون جمع نجي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about their saying may be an implied command to remember or a substitute for the prior time clause; calling them wrongdoers marks their whispered accusation as injustice.
rows.anchor: مقدر باذكر، أو بدل من { إذ هم نجوى } على وضع { الظلمون } موضع الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A bewitched man” may mean someone whose reason has been removed by magic, or a man with lungs who breathes, eats, and drinks like them.
rows.anchor: والمسحور هو الذي سحر فزال عقله. وقيل الذي له سحر وهو الرئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They compare the Prophet to a poet, sorcerer, soothsayer, and madman, straying from truth in every accusation and unable to produce a sound argument or find guidance.
rows.anchor: مثلوك بالشاعر والساحر والكاهن والمجنون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rufāt means fragments; they deny resurrection because living freshness and dry remains seem radically incompatible.
rows.anchor: حطاما. { أإنا لمبعوثون خلقا جديدا } على الإنكار والاستبعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the construction, “when” is governed by the sense of “resurrected,” not by that word itself, since what follows in cannot govern what precedes it; “a new creation” is an infinitive or circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: والعامل في إذا ما دل عليه مبعوثون لا نفسه لأن ما بعد أن لا يعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer challenges them to become stones or iron.
rows.anchor: جوابا لهم. { كونوا حجارة أو حديدا }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may become any form they consider least capable of life; God’s power to revive them is unlimited, and bodies share the capacity to receive accidents.
rows.anchor: أي مما يكبر عندكم عن قبول الحياة لكونه أبعد شيء منها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection is especially clear because they were once living, fresh bodies; what has previously had life is more receptive than what never has.
rows.anchor: فكيف إذا كنتم عظاما مرفوتة وقد كانت غضة موصوفة بالحياة قبل والشيء أقبل لما عهد فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God first created them when they were earth, an even less plausible source of life.
rows.anchor: وكنتم ترابا وما هو أبعد منه من الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They shake their heads toward the Prophet in astonishment and mockery.
rows.anchor: فسيحركونها نحوك تعجبا واستهزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply says the event may be near because everything that is coming is near; “near” may be predicate or adverb, and the clause with an may be the subject or predicate of ʿasā.
rows.anchor: فإن كل ما هو آت قريب، وانتصابه على الخبر أو الظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling and responding are metaphors for resurrection, stressing its speed and ease and that it summons people for reckoning and recompense.
rows.anchor: استعار لهما الدعاء والاستجابة للتنبيه على سرعتهما وتيسر أمرهما، وأن المقصود منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In praise of Him” may describe people praising God for His perfect power, reportedly as they shake dust from their heads and say “Glory to You, God, and praise”; or it means submitting to the summons as one praises it.
rows.anchor: حامدين الله تعالى على كمال قدرته كما قيل إنهم ينفضون التراب عن رؤوسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their brief estimate of their stay may refer to time in the graves, like the passerby at a town, or to their lifetime as they see the terror.
rows.anchor: وتستقصرون مدة لبثكم في القبور كالذي مر على قرية، أو مدة حياتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “My servants” refers to believers, who should say the best words and avoid harshness toward polytheists.
rows.anchor: يعني المؤمنين. { يقولوا التى هى أحسن } الكلمة التي هي أحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan stirs argument and mischief; harsh speech may provoke obstinacy and greater corruption, for Satan is humanity’s manifest enemy.
rows.anchor: يهيج بينهم المراء والشر فلعل المخاشنة بهم تفضي إلى العناد وازدياد الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your Lord knows you” explains the instruction to choose the best words: avoid declaring them hellbound, which provokes evil, since only God knows their final fate.
rows.anchor: تفسير ل { التى هى أحسن } وما بينهما اعتراض أي قولوا لهم هذه الكلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was not made their agent to compel faith but was sent as bearer of good news and warning; he should deal gently and tell companions to be patient with them.
rows.anchor: موكولا إليك أمرهم تقسرهم على الإيمان وإنما أرسلناك مبشرا ونذيرا فدارهم ومر أصحابك بالاحتمال منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported occasion is that the polytheists intensified their abuse, and the Muslims complained to the Messenger, after which the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وروي أن المشركين أفرطوا في إيذائهم فشكوا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فنزلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says a man insulted ʿUmar, who was about to retaliate, and God commanded him to pardon.
rows.anchor: وقيل شتم عمر رضي الله تعالى عنه رجل منهم فهم به فأمره الله بالعفو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the conditions of all in heaven and earth and chooses whom He wills for prophethood and divine friendship; this answers Quraysh’s objection that Abū Ṭālib’s orphan nephew and ragged, hungry companions could be chosen.
rows.anchor: وبأحوالهم فيختار منهم لنبوته وولايته من يشاء، وهو رد لاستبعاد قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets differ in spiritual virtues and freedom from bodily attachments, not wealth or followers; David’s distinction was the revealed book, not his kingdom.
rows.anchor: بالفضائل النفسانية والتبري عن العلائق الجسمانية، لا بكثرة الأموال والأتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view sees a reference to the Prophet’s superiority: David’s Psalms signal that the final Prophet and his community are best, as the Psalms say the righteous will inherit the earth.
rows.anchor: قيل هو إشارة إلى تفضيل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite “Zabūr” here differs from the definite form in 21:105 because the word may be a passive faʿūl, a verbal noun, read with ḍamma by Ḥamza, or may mean a portion of the Psalms, perhaps one mentioning the Messenger.
rows.anchor: وتنكيره ها هنا وتعريفه في قوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beings invoked as gods besides God include angels, the Messiah, and ʿUzayr.
rows.anchor: أنها آلهة. { من دونه } كالملائكة والمسيح وعزير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cannot remove harm such as illness, poverty, or drought, nor transfer it from you to another.
rows.anchor: كالمرض والفقر والقحط. { ولا تحويلا } ولا تحويل ذلك منكم إلى غيركم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those beings called gods themselves seek nearness to God through obedience; the nearest among them seeks the means, so how could a less-near being be divine?
rows.anchor: هؤلاء الآلهة يبتغون إلى الله القرابة بالطاعة. { أيهم أقرب } بدل من واو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They hope for God’s mercy and fear His punishment like all servants, which disproves their divinity.
rows.anchor: كسائر العباد فكيف تزعمون أنهم آلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s punishment is something everyone must fear, including messengers and angels.
rows.anchor: حقيقا بأن يحذره كل أحد حتى الرسل والملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every town will be destroyed before the Resurrection through death or annihilation, or subjected to severe punishment through killing and varied calamities.
rows.anchor: بالموت والاستئصال. { أو معذبوها عذابا شديدا } بالقتل وأنواع البلية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This decree is written in the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: في اللوح المحفوظ. { مسطورا } مكتوبا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God withheld the signs Quraysh requested because He knew they would deny them like ʿĀd and Thamūd, then face annihilation under His established practice; He had decreed not to annihilate Quraysh because some would believe or beget believers.
rows.anchor: ما صرفنا عن إرسال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamūd received the she-camel at their request; it was an evident sign, either seeing clearly, providing insight, or making them insightful, and a reading has fatḥa.
rows.anchor: بسؤالهم. { مبصرة } بينة ذات أبصار أو بصائر، أو جاعلتهم ذوي بصائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They wronged through it” means they disbelieved in the sign or wronged themselves by hamstringing the camel.
rows.anchor: فكفروا بها، أو فظلموا أنفسهم بسبب عقرها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Requested miracles serve as warnings of annihilating punishment; alternatively, unrequested miracles such as Qur’anic signs warn of the afterlife, whose judgment is deferred. The bāʾ may be extra or circumstantial, and the object is omitted.
rows.anchor: من نزول العذاب المستأصل، فإن لم يخافوا نزل أو بغير المقترحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When We told you” means remember when God revealed this to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: واذكر إذ أوحينا إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s encompassing people means they are in His power; alternatively, He encompassed Quraysh by destroying them, a prediction of Badr phrased in the past because it was certain.
rows.anchor: فهم في قبضة قدرته، أو أحاط بقريش بمعنى أهلكهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vision may be the Night Journey, supporting the view it occurred in a dream; those who say it occurred while awake interpret it as seeing.
rows.anchor: ليلة المعراج وتعلق به من قال إنه كان في المنام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may instead be the year of Ḥudaybiyya, when the Prophet saw himself entering Mecca; since the verse is Meccan, this would require that he saw and recounted it in Mecca.
rows.anchor: أو عام الحديبية حين رأى أنه دخل مكة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is a dream before Badr, linked to 8:43 and a report that the Prophet named the Quraysh casualties’ locations at the water, which they heard and mocked.
rows.anchor: ولعله رؤيا رآها في وقعة بدر لقوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the Prophet saw Umayyads climbing his pulpit and leaping like monkeys, and called their worldly allotment a consequence of accepting Islam; on this view, the trial refers to events in their days.
rows.anchor: وقيل رأى قوما من بني أمية يرقون منبره وينزون عليه نزو القردة فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accursed tree is zaqqūm; polytheists mocked the claim that a tree could grow in a Hellfire that burns stones, but God can create a fireproof tree, as nature shows with fire-resistant creatures and swallowed hot iron.
rows.anchor: عطف على { الرءيا } وهي شجرة الزقوم، لما سمع المشركون ذكرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tree is called accursed because its eaters are cursed, by metaphorical intensification; alternatively it grows at Hell’s root far from mercy, or is harmful and loathsome food.
rows.anchor: ولعنها في القرآن لعن طاعميها وصفت به على المجاز للمبالغة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accursed tree has also been interpreted as Satan, Abū Jahl, or al-Ḥakam ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ; a nominative reading treats it as a topic with an omitted predicate meaning “likewise.”
rows.anchor: وقد أولت بالشيطان وأبي جهل والحكم بن أبي العاصي، وقرأت بالرفع على الابتداء
